name: Bread Pakora
instructions: 1. Mash the boiled potatoes and mix with ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, amchur, chili powder, and coriander to create the filling.
2. Spread the potato mixture between two bread slices and cut them into triangles or rectangles.
3. Prepare a thick batter using gram flour, turmeric, carom seeds, salt, and water.
4. Heat oil in a deep pan or kadhai.
5. Dip the stuffed bread pieces into the batter until fully coated.
6. Carefully slide the bread into the hot oil and deep-fry on medium heat until crispy and golden brown on both sides.
7. Drain excess oil on paper towels and serve hot with mint chutney or tamarind sauce.
description: Bread Pakora is an iconic snack found at almost every street corner in Delhi, especially during the monsoon season. It is a quintessential comfort food served by 'thelawalas' and roadside stalls, reflecting the vibrant and indulgent street food culture of the capital.
